headline: Mexico Q3 GDP Grows 0.9% on Quarter, Slowing But Exceeding Expectations
summary: Mexico's third-quarter GDP grew 0.9%. While the rate of growth slowed compared to the second quarter, the expansion came in above expectations.
why: Quarterly gross domestic product figures are primary indicators of economic momentum, closely watched by central bankers and market participants to gauge broader macroeconomic health and future monetary policy.

impacts.name: Mexico
impacts.why: Better-than-expected GDP growth indicates stronger domestic economic activity in Mexico.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: GDP growth coming in above expectations signals stronger-than-anticipated economic resilience, which can support local asset valuations and currency sentiment.
